# Adjudication Task — Chapter 308

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃308화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“사천으로 가거라. 신의라면 분명 방도가 있을 터이니.”
  6|
  7|낙양괴의는 천하에서 열 손가락 안에 드는 명의.
  8|
  9|그런 그가 확신을 담아 말한다. 신의(神醫)를 찾으라고. 그의 의술은 천하제일이라고.
 10|
 11|‘가능성이 보인다.’
 12|
 13|신의를 찾는다면 적천강을 회복시킬 수 있다.
 14|
 15|곤히 잠든 사람처럼 누워 있는 적천강을 바라보던 나는, 낙양괴의를 향해 허리를 숙였다.
 16|
 17|“진심으로 감사드립니다.”
 18|
 19|신의는 누구도 정체를 알 수 없을 만큼 베일에 싸인 인물.
 20|
 21|낙양괴의가 건네준 신의의 증표가 아니었다면 망망대해에 떨어진 기분이었을 것이다.
 22|
 23|“어흠, 입으로만?”
 24|
 25|“기념품이라도 사다 드릴까요?”
 26|
 27|내 장난 섞인 말에 낙양괴의가 피식 웃었다.
 28|
 29|“어린놈이 까불기는. 헛소리 늘어놓을 시간에 당장 행낭이나 꾸려라.”
 30|
 31|“어, 그러네.”
 32|
 33|하남에서 사천까지는 어림잡아도 수천 리 길. 경신법을 발휘한다고 해도 한 달에 가까운 시간이 걸릴 것이 분명했다.
 34|
 35|‘게다가 신의를 금방 찾아낸다는 보장도 없고.’
 36|
 37|나는 아직 닫지 않은 퀘스트창을 바라보며 내심 중얼거렸다.
 38|
 39|
 40|
 41|퀘스트
 42|
 43|
 44|
 45|[사천에서 신 서방 찾기]
 46|
 47|
 48|
 49|당신은 신의가 남긴 유일한 흔적을 습득했습니다.
 50|
 51|신의는 천하제일의 명의. 현재로서는 그만이 적천강을 깨울 수 있는 유일한 희망입니다.
 52|
 53|드넓은 사천 땅을 샅샅이 뒤져서라도 찾아내야 합니다!
 54|
 55|
 56|
 57|등급 : 초절정
 58|
 59|제한 : [신의의 흔적]을 지닌 자
 60|
 61|임무 : 신의를 찾아 진료받기 (미완료)
 62|
 63|보상 : ???
 64|
 65|실패 : 적천강의 죽음
 66|
 67|
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|퀘스트 등급 꼬라지 보소.
 72|
 73|사람 하나 찾는 건데 등급이 무려 초절정이다.
 74|
 75|다행히 그가 오래전에 남긴 흔적을 통해 사천이라는 소재지를 파악할 수 있었지만, 워낙 땅덩어리가 넓다 보니 그마저도 더럽게 빡세다.
 76|
 77|‘현대의 쓰촨성이 한반도 면적의 두 배 정도던가?’
 78|
 79|무림과 현대는 완전히 분리된 다른 세계. 그러나 지금까지 경험한 바로는 땅의 크기와 사람들의 생활 등, 양식은 비슷했다.
 80|
 81|그런 사천에서 이름도, 얼굴도 모르는 누군가를 찾는다고 생각하니 막막하다.
 82|
 83|‘시벌, 차라리 서울에서 김 서방 찾는 게 더 쉽겠다.’
 84|
 85|하지만 별수 있나. 이건 선택의 문제가 아니다. 반드시, 무슨 수를 써서라도 신의를 찾아야 적천강이 살 수 있다.
 86|
 87|남은 시간은 반년.
 88|
 89|꾸준히 추궁과혈을 해 준다면 한두 달 정도를 벌 수 있겠지만 그것이 적천강에게 허락된 시간의 전부였다.
 90|
 91|‘기한 안에 반드시 찾아낸다.’
 92|
 93|그러기 위해서는 필요한 시간을 단축해야 한다. 빠르게 머리를 굴린 내가 입을 열었다.
 94|
 95|“부탁 하나 드려도 됩니까?”
 96|
 97|막대한 인력과 자금이 소모될지도 모르는 일.
 98|
 99|그러나 검성 매종학은 망설임 없이 해결책을 제시했다.
100|
101|“사천의 당문(唐門)과 아미(峨嵋), 청성(峨嵋)에 보내는 서신을 적어 주지.”
102|
103|“감사합니다.”
104|
105|오대세가의 일원인 사천당문. 거기에 더해 각기 구파일방의 한 축을 담당하는 아미파와 청성파의 협조까지 얻는다면 일이 훨씬 수월해질 수 있을 것이다.
106|
107|하지만 내 부탁은 거기에서 끝이 아니었다.
108|
109|“기왕 도와주시는 김에 몇 가지만 더 추가해 주실 수 있습니까?”
110|
111|“음, 소림에서 일어난 혈사(血史)로 분위기가 흉흉하네. 모두가 암천과 마교의 준동을 생각하는 터라 그리 큰 도움은 줄 수 없을지 몰라. 문파에 적을 둔 무림인에게는 사문이 최우선이니 말일세.”
112|
113|“그 정도로 큰 도움까지는 필요 없습니다.”
114|
115|“내가, 화산이 도울 수 있는 것이라면 뭐든 말해 보게.”
116|
117|“사람 몇 명만 붙여 주세요. 그거면 됩니다.”
118|
119|“생각해 둔 인물이 있나?”
120|
121|“네.”
122|
123|고개를 끄덕인 나는 몇 사람의 이름을 말했다.
124|
125|
126|
127|* * *
128|
129|
130|
131|잠시 후, 전각을 나선 매종학과 낙양괴의는 천천히 걸음을 옮기며 대화를 나눴다.
132|
133|“괜찮겠나? 신의를 만나는 것이 자네의 일생 소원으로 알고 있는데.”
134|
135|“일생의 소원이라…….”
136|
137|매종학의 말에 낙양괴의가 아련한 눈빛으로 옛 기억을 떠올렸다.
138|
139|“그랬지요. 관직도 때려치우고 침을 든 것이 그분 때문이었으니 말입니다.”
140|
141|낙양괴의는 한때 전도유망한 서생이었다.
142|
143|그의 조부는 최고의 교육 기관인 국자감(國子監)의 수장이었고 선황의 태자 시절 스승이기도 했다.
144|
145|학사의 핏줄이 어디로 가겠는가, 그의 아버지도, 두 형도 조정에 출사하여 이름을 떨쳤다.
146|
147|낙양괴의가 장원 급제한 그 해, 역병이 일어나지 않았다면 아마 그 또한 같은 전철을 밟았을 것이다.
148|
149|“헤아릴 수 없이 많은 이들이 명을 달리했습니다. 저는 맡은 소임에 따라 죽은 자와 살아남은 자, 그리고 죽어야 할 이들을 분류했지요.”
150|
151|이제 막 조정에 출사한 젊은 시절의 낙양괴의는 믿어 의심치 않았다.
152|
153|지엄하신 황상께서 명을 내려 구휼미를 풀고, 어의들을 보내어 역병을 잠재울 것을. 문무백관이 고통받는 백성들을 살리기 위해 최선을 다할 것임을.
154|
155|“착각이었습니다. 백성들이 역병으로 죽어 가던 그때, 황상은 새로 들인 후궁을 위해 별궁을 중축했고 백성들에게 가야 할 것들은 힘 있는 자들이 나누어 가졌습니다.”
156|
157|“자네는 어찌했나?”
158|
159|“거짓을 사실로 바꾸어 적었습니다. 제 붓끝에서 십만 석의 양곡과 재물, 약재는 병자들에게 베풀어진 것이 되었고 사대부들의 곁을 지키던 황실 어의들은 역병을 잠재우기 위해 애쓰는 참된 의원이 되었습니다.”
160|
161|“괴로웠겠군.”
162|
163|“고통스러웠습니다. 퇴궐 후 가문에 돌아오니 황상이 보낸 어의들이 있더군요. 가벼운 고뿔에 걸린 조부를 위해 보낸 이들이었습니다.”
164|
165|그때 처음 알았다. 목숨에도 값어치를 매기는 세상이라는 것을.
166|
167|침구가 든 보자기를 움켜쥔 낙양괴의의 손이 하얗게 물들었다.
168|
169|“그러던 차에 신의에 관한 소식을 들었지요. 죽음을 무릅쓰고 역병의 근원지에서 병자를 치료하는 의원. 홀로 역병을 잠재우고 수천의 인명을 살린 한 사람.”
170|
171|그는 즉시 입궐하여 자신이 쓴 기록을 모두 없앤 후 조정을 떠났다. 가문과 연을 끊어야 했지만 상관없었다.
172|
173|붓 대신 침을 들었고, 사서삼경(四書三經)이 아닌 의서(醫書)를 탐독했다.
174|
175|“돌팔이라고 욕도 많이 먹었지요. 죽음의 문턱에 앉아 있던 병자를 살린 적도 있었고, 끝내 치료하지 못해 떠나보낸 적도 많았습니다.”
176|
177|의원이 된 그는 수많은 생로병사(生老病死)를 지켜보았다.
178|
179|그리고 그로부터 이십 년이라는 세월이 흐른 후, 촉망받던 젊은 관료는 낙양괴의라는 이름으로 불리기 시작했다.
180|
181|“모두 신의가 있었기에 가능했던 일입니다. 그가 아니었다면 저는 썩어 빠진 조정의 꼭두각시가 되었을 테니 말입니다.”
182|
183|낙양괴의의 말에 매종학이 빙긋 웃었다.
184|
185|“신의가 또 다른 신의를 낳았군.”
186|
187|“무슨 당치 않은 말씀을. 소인은 괴의로 만족하렵니다. 신의는 세상천지에 오직 한 명뿐이니까요.”
188|
189|괴팍하기로 유명한 낙양괴의의 눈동자는 소년의 그것처럼 반짝반짝 빛나고 있었다.
190|
191|그 모습에 매종학은 참지 못하고 실소를 흘렸다.
192|
193|“이것 참. 지금이라도 신의의 증표를 되돌려 받아야 하는 것 아닌가?”
194|
195|“하늘은 닿을 수 없기에 하늘인 것. 그분을 찾고자 했다면 증표를 받은 십 년 전 이미 사천으로 떠났겠지요. 제 자리는 이곳입니다. 그리고…….”
196|
197|낙양괴의가 씁쓸한 미소와 함께 덧붙였다.
198|
199|“이 나이에도 환자 하나 고치지 못하는 돌팔이가 무슨 낯짝으로 신의를 뵙겠습니까? 이것으로 되었습니다.”
200|
201|“고맙네. 무리가 들끓는 지금, 적 대협이 회생한다면 무림 전체가 자네에게 큰 빚을 진 셈이야.”
202|
203|“어허, 왜 이러십니까? 안 어울리게.”
204|
205|너스레를 떨며 손을 내젓던 낙양괴의의 얼굴에 문득 짓궂은 표정이 떠올랐다.
206|
207|“혹시 미리 연습하시는 겁니까?”
208|
209|“연습이라니?”
210|
211|“무림 맹주로서의 무게감 말입니다, 하하.”
212|
213|“아, 그거 말인가?”
214|
215|매종학이 떨떠름한 얼굴로 뒤통수를 긁적였다.
216|
217|“도대체 누가 그런 말을 퍼트리고 다니는지 모르겠군. 이미 몇 차례나 거절한 일인데…….”
218|
219|“지금으로서는 매 대협께서 적격이시지요.”
220|
221|“그런 말 마시게. 모두 마음이 조급해서 잘못된 선택을 하는 것뿐이야.”
222|
223|소림사에서 있었던 혈사는 위험을 알리는 경종이었다.
224|
225|암천이라 불리는 암중 세력의 등장.
226|
227|지금까지 밝혀진 바 없는 적이 모습을 드러내자 정파 무림 수뇌부는 조심스럽게 한 가지 주제를 입에 담기 시작했다.
228|
229|바로 무림맹(武林盟)의 재결성이었다.
230|
231|“그 자리가 어울리는 사람은 따로 있네. 적어도 노부는 아니지.”
232|
233|“그렇게 생각하십니까?”
234|
235|낙양괴의는 손을 뻗어 하늘을 가리켰다.
236|
237|아직 이른 새벽. 이제 막 동이 튼 하늘에는 아직 달과 별이 남아 있었다.
238|
239|“일신(日神)은 모습을 감췄고, 십왕(十王)은 늙었습니다. 제 눈으로 본 매 대협께서는 고강한 무공과 올바른 마음을 갖춘 분이십니다. 정파의 상징인 무림맹을 맡기에 가장 적합한 분이시지요.”
240|
241|“사람 참. 노부는 절대 안 된다니까. 사람이 얼마나 많은데 나를 무림 맹주로 세운단 말인가?”
242|
243|“그럼 누가 적합하다고 보십니까?”
244|
245|“음…….”
246|
247|잠시 고민하던 매종학이 입을 열었다.
248|
249|“그렇지. 당장 가까이로 벽력도왕 팽 선배가 계시잖나.”
250|
251|“맹주를 하시기에는 성미가 너무.”
252|
253|“응? 팽 선배가 어때서. 나는 화끈하고 좋던데. 사내답고.”
254|
255|“무림맹도 화끈하게 말아먹을 것 같습니다. 사내답게.”
256|
257|“그럼 제갈공후 선배가 적격이지. 과거 무림맹 총군사 직을 맡기도 하셨고, 초절정의 선법과 뛰어난 진법으로 십왕에 오르신…….”
258|
259|“돌아가셨습니다.”
260|
261|“헉. 언제 말인가?”
262|
263|“십 년도 넘었지요.”
264|
265|“허어…….”
266|
267|하도 오랜만에 나왔더니 누가 살았는지 죽었는지조차 제대로 알지 못한다.
268|
269|침음성을 흘리던 매종학이 물었다.
270|
271|“혹시 삼성의 다른 두 사람은 어찌 되었는지 알고 있나?”
272|
273|“궁성(弓星)께서도 이십여 년 전부터 종적이 묘연하시고, 다른 한 분은…… 솔직히 논외로 쳐야지요.”
274|
275|“응? 어째서 말인가?”
276|
277|낙양괴의가 어처구니없다는 표정으로 매종학을 바라봤다.
278|
279|“도대체 누가 살성(殺星)을 무림 맹주로 추대하려 하겠습니까?”
280|
281|“그 친구가 뭐 어때서? 무공이야 말할 것도 없고, 성격도 철저하니 맹주로 딱이구먼.”
282|
283|“그 무공과 철저한 성격으로 살수 짓을 하니 문제인 게지요. 천하제일의 살수가 무림 맹주라니. 가당키나 합니까?”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

A short while later, Mae Jonghak and the Luoyang Strange Physician left the pavilion and talked as they walked.

[P49]
“Are you certain about this? I understand that meeting the Divine Physician has been your lifelong wish.”

[P50]
“My lifelong wish…”

[P51]
The Luoyang Strange Physician’s gaze grew distant as he recalled the past.

[P52]
“It was. He was the reason I abandoned my official post and took up acupuncture needles.”

[P53]
The Luoyang Strange Physician had once been a promising young scholar.

[P54]
His grandfather had been the head of the Guozijian, the empire’s highest educational institution, and had served as the late Emperor’s tutor when he was Crown Prince.

[P55]
A scholar’s blood ran true. His father and two older brothers had also entered government service and made names for themselves at court.

[P56]

[P57]

[P59]

“What did you do?”

[P66]

[P69]

[P70]

[P71]

[P73]
Twenty years later, the promising young official had become known as the Luoyang Strange Physician.

[P74]

[P76]

[P87]

[P92]

“More than ten years ago.”

[P116]
“Good heavens…”

[P119]

[P120]
“Hm? Why not?”

[P122]

[P123]

[P125]
“Is that so? Now that you mention it, you may have a point.”

[P126]

[P127]

[P128]

[P131]
“My youngest.”

[P132]

[P133]
“Yes?”

[P134]
“This eldest brother has just heard something unbelievable.”

[P135]
“Believe it. It’s true.”

“W-where did you say you were going?”

“Sichuan.”

[P140]
“No!”

[P142]
“How can you leave again at a dangerous time like this?”

[P143]
“I’m going to Sichuan.”

[P144]
“I know! That is why I cannot let you go!”

[P145]
“I’m still going.”

[P146]

[P147]

[P148]

[P149]
“What happens if I do?”

[P150]
“I will have no choice but to punish you according to family law.”

[P151]
“Then strike me from the family register.”

[P152]
“How can you say such a thing?”

[P153]
From the look on his face, the world was going to end in ten minutes.

[P154]

[P155]
Jeok Cheongang, still unconscious, was secured to the wooden back carrier on my back with silk.

[P156]
*It might be too late if I find the Divine Physician and bring him all the way back here.*

[P157]
That was why I’d chosen this method.

[P158]
I would take Jeok Cheongang to Sichuan with me.

[P159]
“Heave-ho.”

[P160]
This should hold well enough for me to use my movement technique, at least to some extent.

[P161]
I let out a deep sigh at the pleading look in Jin Wikyung’s eyes.

[P162]
“Don’t worry so much. Nothing like what you’re imagining is going to happen.”

[P163]
“Take the Jin Dragon Squad. At least take the Jin Dragon Squad with you.”

[P164]
The Jin Dragon Squad might be the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most elite force, but right now they’d only be deadweight slowing me down.

[P165]
I tossed my fully packed traveling bag to one of the men nearby.

[P166]
“That’s why I’m taking the Vice Squad Leader with me.”

[P167]
Hyuk Mujin caught the bag and thumped his chest confidently.

[P168]
“Leave it all to me, Lesser Family Head!”

[P169]
“…”

[P170]
“…Lesser Family Head?”

[P171]
“Ah, it’s nothing. Please take good care of my youngest.”

[P172]
Jin Wikyung patted Hyuk Mujin on the shoulder, looking as if he trusted him about as far as he could throw him.

[P173]
That was when—

[P174]
“Benefactor! When are we leaving? Huh? Benefactor?”

[P175]
“…”

[P176]
“We’re leaving now, so please shut your mouth.”

[P177]
Was bringing that guy really the right decision?

[P178]
A sudden wave of regret hit me, but Cheongpung was perfect for this mission, which required a small, elite group.

[P179]
*At least there’s no questioning his strength.*

[P180]
If anything went wrong on the journey, Cheongpung alone would be worth an army.

[P181]
“Sichuan! The Divine Physician! This is so exciting!”

[P182]
“…”

[P183]
It still wasn’t too late. Maybe I should just leave him behind.

[P184]
Locked in a fierce internal struggle, I left the pavilion.

[P185]
The final member of our party was waiting at the entrance.

[P186]
“Long time no see.”

[P187]
At my greeting, he answered with a gloomy expression.

[P188]
“Requesting me was a poor choice.”

[P189]
“No. You have to come with us.”

[P190]
“My Myriad-Li Chasing Wind Movement Technique…”

[P191]
“You only learned it to the fifth stage.”

[P192]
“H-how do you know that?”

[P193]
“…Have you learned anything past the fifth stage?”

[P194]
*The Oseong-and-Haneum villain.*[^1]

[P195]
No, the final member was Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect.

[P196]
Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung, and Gung Gibang.

[P197]
Now that I saw the three of them together, this lineup was no joke.

[P198]
I sighed.

[P199]
“All right, let’s go, you three Bermuda Triangle bastards.”

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 308

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃308화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“사천으로 가거라. 신의라면 분명 방도가 있을 터이니.”
  6|
  7|낙양괴의는 천하에서 열 손가락 안에 드는 명의.
  8|
  9|그런 그가 확신을 담아 말한다. 신의(神醫)를 찾으라고. 그의 의술은 천하제일이라고.
 10|
 11|‘가능성이 보인다.’
 12|
 13|신의를 찾는다면 적천강을 회복시킬 수 있다.
 14|
 15|곤히 잠든 사람처럼 누워 있는 적천강을 바라보던 나는, 낙양괴의를 향해 허리를 숙였다.
 16|
 17|“진심으로 감사드립니다.”
 18|
 19|신의는 누구도 정체를 알 수 없을 만큼 베일에 싸인 인물.
 20|
 21|낙양괴의가 건네준 신의의 증표가 아니었다면 망망대해에 떨어진 기분이었을 것이다.
 22|
 23|“어흠, 입으로만?”
 24|
 25|“기념품이라도 사다 드릴까요?”
 26|
 27|내 장난 섞인 말에 낙양괴의가 피식 웃었다.
 28|
 29|“어린놈이 까불기는. 헛소리 늘어놓을 시간에 당장 행낭이나 꾸려라.”
 30|
 31|“어, 그러네.”
 32|
 33|하남에서 사천까지는 어림잡아도 수천 리 길. 경신법을 발휘한다고 해도 한 달에 가까운 시간이 걸릴 것이 분명했다.
 34|
 35|‘게다가 신의를 금방 찾아낸다는 보장도 없고.’
 36|
 37|나는 아직 닫지 않은 퀘스트창을 바라보며 내심 중얼거렸다.
 38|
 39|
 40|
 41|퀘스트
 42|
 43|
 44|
 45|[사천에서 신 서방 찾기]
 46|
 47|
 48|
 49|당신은 신의가 남긴 유일한 흔적을 습득했습니다.
 50|
 51|신의는 천하제일의 명의. 현재로서는 그만이 적천강을 깨울 수 있는 유일한 희망입니다.
 52|
 53|드넓은 사천 땅을 샅샅이 뒤져서라도 찾아내야 합니다!
 54|
 55|
 56|
 57|등급 : 초절정
 58|
 59|제한 : [신의의 흔적]을 지닌 자
 60|
 61|임무 : 신의를 찾아 진료받기 (미완료)
 62|
 63|보상 : ???
 64|
 65|실패 : 적천강의 죽음
 66|
 67|
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|퀘스트 등급 꼬라지 보소.
 72|
 73|사람 하나 찾는 건데 등급이 무려 초절정이다.
 74|
 75|다행히 그가 오래전에 남긴 흔적을 통해 사천이라는 소재지를 파악할 수 있었지만, 워낙 땅덩어리가 넓다 보니 그마저도 더럽게 빡세다.
 76|
 77|‘현대의 쓰촨성이 한반도 면적의 두 배 정도던가?’
 78|
 79|무림과 현대는 완전히 분리된 다른 세계. 그러나 지금까지 경험한 바로는 땅의 크기와 사람들의 생활 등, 양식은 비슷했다.
 80|
 81|그런 사천에서 이름도, 얼굴도 모르는 누군가를 찾는다고 생각하니 막막하다.
 82|
 83|‘시벌, 차라리 서울에서 김 서방 찾는 게 더 쉽겠다.’
 84|
 85|하지만 별수 있나. 이건 선택의 문제가 아니다. 반드시, 무슨 수를 써서라도 신의를 찾아야 적천강이 살 수 있다.
 86|
 87|남은 시간은 반년.
 88|
 89|꾸준히 추궁과혈을 해 준다면 한두 달 정도를 벌 수 있겠지만 그것이 적천강에게 허락된 시간의 전부였다.
 90|
 91|‘기한 안에 반드시 찾아낸다.’
 92|

[P66]

[P69]
He had to sever all ties with his family, but he didn’t care.

[P70]
He traded his brush for acupuncture needles and studied medical texts instead of the Four Books and Three Classics.

[P71]
“I was called a quack more times than I can count. Sometimes I saved patients already sitting at death’s door. Many other times, I failed to cure them and had to watch them go.”

As a physician, he witnessed the countless cycles of birth, aging, illness, and death.

[P73]
Twenty years later, the promising young official had become known as the Luoyang Strange Physician.

[P74]
“None of it would have been possible without the Divine Physician. Without him, I would have become a puppet of that rotten court.”

[P76]

[P90]

[P92]

[P94]

The bloodbath at Shaolin Temple had sounded the alarm.

[P96]
A hidden force known as Dark Heaven had emerged.

[P97]

The re-formation of the Murim Alliance.

[P99]
“Someone else is better suited to the position. At the very least, this old man is not.”

[P100]
“Do you truly believe that?”

[P101]
The Luoyang Strange Physician raised a hand and pointed toward the sky.

[P102]

[P103]
“One God has vanished, and the Ten Kings have grown old. From what I have seen with my own eyes, Great Hero Mae possesses both formidable martial arts and an upright heart. You are the man best suited to lead the Murim Alliance, the symbol of the orthodox faction.”

[P104]

[P106]
“Hm…”

Mae Jonghak thought for a moment before answering.

[P109]
“His temperament is far too…”

“What’s wrong with Senior Peng? I like that fiery personality of his. He’s manly.”

[P111]
“He would make a fiery wreck of the Murim Alliance. In the manliest way possible.”

[P116]
“Good heavens…”

Mae Jonghak had been away for so long that he no longer knew who was alive and who was dead.

[P120]
“Hm? Why not?”

[P122]

[P123]

[P125]

[P131]
“My youngest.”

[P132]

[P133]
“Yes?”

[P134]
“This eldest brother has just heard something unbelievable.”

[P135]
“Believe it. It’s true.”

[P136]
“W-where did you say you were going?”

[P137]
“Sichuan.”

[P138]
“H-how long will you be gone?”

[P139]
“Six months. Maybe another month or two if it takes longer.”

[P140]
“No!”

[P141]

[P142]
“How can you leave again at a dangerous time like this?”

[P143]
“I’m going to Sichuan.”

[P144]
“I know! That is why I cannot let you go!”

[P145]
“I’m still going.”

[P146]

[P147]

[P149]
“What happens if I do?”

[P150]
“I will have no choice but to punish you according to family law.”

[P151]
“Then strike me from the family register.”

[P152]
“How can you say such a thing?”

[P153]
From the look on his face, the world was going to end in ten minutes.

[P154]

[P155]
Jeok Cheongang, still unconscious, was secured to the wooden back carrier on my back with silk.

[P156]
*It might be too late if I find the Divine Physician and bring him all the way back here.*

[P157]
That was why I’d chosen this method.

[P158]
I would take Jeok Cheongang to Sichuan with me.

[P159]
“Heave-ho.”

[P160]
This should hold well enough for me to use my movement technique, at least to some extent.

[P161]
I let out a deep sigh at the pleading look in Jin Wikyung’s eyes.

[P162]
“Don’t worry so much. Nothing like what you’re imagining is going to happen.”

[P163]
“Take the Jin Dragon Squad. At least take the Jin Dragon Squad with you.”

[P164]
The Jin Dragon Squad might be the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most elite force, but right now they’d only be deadweight slowing me down.

[P165]
I tossed my fully packed traveling bag to one of the men nearby.

[P166]
“That’s why I’m taking the Vice Squad Leader with me.”

[P167]
Hyuk Mujin caught the bag and thumped his chest confidently.

[P168]
“Leave it all to me, Lesser Family Head!”

[P169]
“…”

[P170]
“…Lesser Family Head?”

[P171]
“Ah, it’s nothing. Please take good care of my youngest.”

[P172]
Jin Wikyung patted Hyuk Mujin on the shoulder, looking as if he trusted him about as far as he could throw him.

[P173]
That was when—

[P174]
“Benefactor! When are we leaving? Huh? Benefactor?”

[P175]
“…”

[P176]
“We’re leaving now, so please shut your mouth.”

[P177]
Was bringing that guy really the right decision?

[P178]
A sudden wave of regret hit me, but Cheongpung was perfect for this mission, which required a small, elite group.

[P179]
*At least there’s no questioning his strength.*

[P180]
If anything went wrong on the journey, Cheongpung alone would be worth an army.

[P181]
“Sichuan! The Divine Physician! This is so exciting!”

[P182]
“…”

[P183]
It still wasn’t too late. Maybe I should just leave him behind.

[P184]
Locked in a fierce internal struggle, I left the pavilion.

[P185]
The final member of our party was waiting at the entrance.

[P186]
“Long time no see.”

[P187]
At my greeting, he answered with a gloomy expression.

[P188]
“Requesting me was a poor choice.”

[P189]
“No. You have to come with us.”

[P190]
“My Myriad-Li Chasing Wind Movement Technique…”

[P191]
“You only learned it to the fifth stage.”

[P192]
“H-how do you know that?”

[P193]
“…Have you learned anything past the fifth stage?”

[P194]
*The Oseong-and-Haneum villain.*[^1]

[P195]
No, the final member was Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect.

[P196]
Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung, and Gung Gibang.

[P197]
Now that I saw the three of them together, this lineup was no joke.

[P198]
I sighed.

[P199]
“All right, let’s go, you three Bermuda Triangle bastards.”

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
